name: rmlinks
description: rm -r removes a symbolic link, not what it points to, as 2.11BSD's rm does with lstat(2) (usr/bin/rm.c:92) (apple/fgx#530).  d holds a symlink to the directory keep; `rm -r d' must take d and the link and leave keep/f, which cat then reads.  The ProDOS-era port stat(2)ed, so the link looked like a directory, rm descended through it and deleted keep/f before failing on the link itself; `kept' would never print.  A probe, not a gate test.
command: cd /tmp; mkdir keep d; P=ke; X=pt; echo $P$X > keep/f; ln -s ../keep d/l; rm -r d; echo rm=$?; cat keep/f; rm -r keep; sync
